note: Registry of every paid campaign, on-platform and off. A campaign must exist here before `python3 hub.py ads log` will accept spend against it, so no dollar ever lands in the ledger without a named owner, a target, a stated hypothesis and a kill rule with a number in it. Mechanics and benchmarks are verified in research/marketplace-expansion.md section 4. Every field still marked TODO is genuinely unknown: fill it by reading the real platform, or leave it.
naming_convention: <channel>-<target>-<variant>. channel: fvr, upw, meta, gads, li. target: gig ref, vertical, or mechanism. variant optional: us, retarget, default, test-b. The id is permanent once spend has been logged against it, because renaming breaks the series.

campaigns.objective: Buy the keyword analytics that show which search terms buyers actually used to reach the gigs, and settle the tool-keyword versus vertical-keyword question with evidence rather than argument.
campaigns.hypothesis: By day 10 the keyword report will show whether impressions are arriving on vertical terms (car dealership, insurance agency) or tool terms (vapi, retell). If vertical dominates, the positioning is confirmed and no tag changes. If tool dominates, one tag on gig1 swaps toward tool language.
campaigns.eligibility: Confirmed available. Kickstart is exclusively for new freelancers who have not yet received a Fiverr level, which is us.
campaigns.budget_note: $15/month. Refundable if cancelled within 48 hours of the last monthly payment.
campaigns.audience: n/a, this is a tooling subscription
campaigns.kill_rule: Cancel at the end of month 1 if the keyword report has produced no tag or title decision. It buys no ranking and nobody should report one.

campaigns.objective: 100 Connects a month plus competitor bid visibility on the bidding account, and the 0% service fee on self-brought clients.
campaigns.hypothesis: Competitor bid visibility changes at least one bid per week away from the 95% to 105% of posted budget band, which replies at 8.8%, the worst position measured.
campaigns.budget_note: $19.99/month, including 100 Connects worth $15. Net marginal cost about $5. Also unlocks the one-time 50-Connect new-freelancer bonus, which only arrives after purchasing Connects or subscribing.
campaigns.kill_rule: Cancel if fewer than 60 proposals are sent in a month, because at that volume the 100 Connects are not being used and the subscription is not paying for itself.

campaigns.objective: Structural, not growth. Agency Plus is required before Frankie can be added as a business manager, which is the whole legitimate basis for a US-facing sales lead bidding on work an India-based engineer delivers.
campaigns.hypothesis: Not a hypothesis. This is a structural cost of the compliant account structure.
campaigns.eligibility: Requires an agency, which requires a freelancer account. One agency per freelancer.
campaigns.budget_note: about $19.99/month. Unlocks the ability to buy Connects; it does not hand any over.
campaigns.kill_rule: None. Cancelling removes Frankie's business-manager seat, which removes the structure. This line is not optional while the agency exists.

campaigns.objective: Buy the proposal volume the first-hire planning number requires: 30 to 50 high-signal proposals over 3 to 5 weeks.
campaigns.hypothesis: At 10 Connects per proposal and a 13.77% interview rate from the full template, 40 proposals produce 5 to 6 interviews and at least one hire inside 5 weeks.
campaigns.bid_model: $0.15 per Connect. 8 to 10 Connects on a standard job, 12 to 16 on large or featured jobs.
campaigns.budget_note: Tier A: 400 Connects, $60. Tier B: 1,000 total, $150. Connects are refunded only if the client cancels the job before any contract forms or Upwork removes the post. Not for a rejected, outbid, expired or withdrawn proposal.
campaigns.audience: Jobs inside the eight ranked niches, posted in the last hour, payment verified, budget $1,000+
campaigns.kill_rule: Stop buying Connects if the interview rate is below 5% over 20 proposals. Rewrite the opening two lines and the Loom first. Connects spent against a broken template is the most wasteful line in the whole plan.

campaigns.objective: Put a proposal into one of the four boosted slots at the top of the client's proposal list, on high-value jobs only.
campaigns.hypothesis: Boosted proposals on $1,500+ jobs with named vertical proof produce a higher interview rate than organic proposals on comparable jobs, measured over 20 boosted sends.
campaigns.eligibility: Open to any freelancer with Connects.
campaigns.bid_model: Connects auction, four slots. You can bid any Connects amount. The auction settles on your own bid, not the runner-up's. You pay only if you are in the top four at close or the client interacts. Only the boost Connects are refundable; the standard submission Connects are not.
campaigns.budget_note: Cap 30 Connects ($4.50) per boost, at most 25% of proposals. Tier A: about 14 boosts, $35. Tier B: about 44 boosts, $148. Keep boost spend under 2% of expected contract value.
campaigns.audience: $1,500+ jobs only, inside a niche where we hold named vertical proof. Never a job we would not personally want.
campaigns.kill_rule: Stop boosting if boosted interviews do not exceed organic interviews over 20 boosted proposals. The Stats and trends page shows the boosted versus organic split.

campaigns.objective: Show 'Available now' on the profile and in search results, and be findable by clients filtering for it when sending invitations.
campaigns.hypothesis: The badge produces at least one invitation inside 14 days. Invited jobs convert better than bid jobs because the shortlist is shorter.
campaigns.bid_model: Connects, floating price. Upwork states there is no maximum price for the badge, but the freelancer sets a personal Connects spending cap and the badge is removed automatically when the cap is reached.
campaigns.budget_note: Hard cap 100 Connects, about $15, per month for the first 60 days.
campaigns.audience: Clients sending invitations who filter for available freelancers
campaigns.kill_rule: Zero invitations received across 14 days of badge spend: turn it off. Invitations are read from Stats and trends.

campaigns.objective: Capture existing purchase intent that never reaches a marketplace at all, on exact-match long-tail commercial queries, and land it on the Gig 1 URL during the honeymoon window.
campaigns.hypothesis: Exact-match 'ai receptionist for car dealership' and 'ai phone agent insurance agency' clear at a CPC nearer the automotive $2.27 than the B2B SaaS $8.50 to $14.00, because almost nobody bids on a four-word intent phrase in this category. A week of the search-terms report proves or disproves it.
campaigns.bid_model: CPC auction, exact match, manual CPC with a ceiling until there is conversion data
campaigns.budget_note: Tier A: $135 over about 4 weeks at $4.80/day, roughly 59 clicks at $2.27. Tier B: $300 at about $10/day. Tier C: part of $900 at about $30/day across three ad groups. Benchmarks: Automotive CPC $2.27, CTR 8.28%, CVR 6.01%, CPL $44.26. Business Services CPC $5.87, CTR 6.10%, CVR 4.85%, CPL $93.69.
campaigns.audience: Exact-match keywords: 'ai receptionist for car dealership', 'ai phone agent insurance agency', 'ai voice agent for dealership bdc'. The real keyword list gets rebuilt from the search-terms report in week 1, not invented here.
campaigns.creative: Text ads. Headlines pull from the gig image headlines so the message is identical on both surfaces. See ads/creative-briefs.md, briefs 1 and 3.
campaigns.landing: The Fiverr Gig 1 URL. Never a phone number, never an email, never an off-platform payment path.
campaigns.kill_rule: Pause if 7 days of spend produce clicks and zero messages, or if cost per message exceeds 10% of the $450 Basic price, meaning $45. Pause immediately on any day with spend and zero clicks.

campaigns.objective: A separate ad group at a lower bid on the compliance query set, which is anxiety-driven and where an entire vendor content industry exists off-platform while on-platform supply mentions consent nowhere.
campaigns.hypothesis: Compliance queries convert to messages at a lower cost per message than the receptionist queries, because the searcher is further along and more worried.
campaigns.bid_model: CPC auction, exact and phrase match, bid below the gads-search-intent group
campaigns.budget_note: Part of the Tier B $300 and the Tier C $900. Separate ad group so its cost per message is separately readable.
campaigns.audience: 'tcpa compliant ai calling', 'ai cold calling compliance', 'dnc scrubbing ai dialer'
campaigns.kill_rule: Same as gads-search-intent: 7 days of clicks with zero messages, or cost per message above $35, which is 10% of the $350 Audit price.
campaigns.compliance_note: Educational framing only. Not legal advice. Never imply US bar admission.

campaigns.objective: Off-platform traffic into the Gig 1 URL during and after the honeymoon window, from an audience marketplace search never reaches.
campaigns.hypothesis: At a $2.52 B2B CPC, $200 buys about 79 clicks, and dealership decision-makers click the missed-call framing at a higher rate than the latency framing. Two creatives, one variable.
campaigns.eligibility: n/a. Fiverr explicitly permits paid advertising on Facebook and Instagram to a gig URL: 'Sharing a link to your Gig or profile is encouraged.'
campaigns.bid_model: CPC or CPM auction, lowest cost, conversions objective once a pixel exists
campaigns.budget_note: Tier B: $200. Tier C: $600. Benchmarks: Meta B2B CPC $2.52, B2B SaaS CPL $63.40, Professional Services CPL $72.40.
campaigns.audience: US car dealership decision makers: dealer principals, general managers, BDC managers, fixed operations directors, franchise and independent rooftops. The exact interest and job-title configuration gets recorded here once the ad account exists and the options have been read off the real interface.
campaigns.creative: Gig 1 images at research/gig-images/gig1-*.png plus the missed-call reel. See ads/creative-briefs.md, briefs 1 and 5.
campaigns.kill_rule: Pause if 7 days of spend produce clicks and zero messages, or cost per message above $45. Pause immediately on spend with zero clicks.
campaigns.compliance_note: Label AI-generated media where platform policy requires. No client name, no dealership name, no dialed number visible or spoken.

campaigns.objective: Reach US insurance agency owners with the TCPA angle, which is the widest demand-to-supply gap found anywhere in the research and has no on-platform supply at all.
campaigns.hypothesis: The compliance framing produces a lower cost per lead than the dealership framing, because Meta Financial Services CPL benchmarks at $58.70 against $72.40 for Professional Services, and the anxiety is specific.
campaigns.bid_model: CPC or CPM auction, lead form or link click
campaigns.budget_note: Tier B: part of $200. Tier C: part of $600. Offer is the free Compliance-Safe AI Audit.
campaigns.audience: US independent insurance agency owners and principals, plus agency operations managers.
campaigns.creative: Gig 2 images at research/gig-images/gig2-*.png plus the compliance reel. See ads/creative-briefs.md, briefs 2 and 6.
campaigns.kill_rule: Same as meta-dealers-us. Cost per message above $35 or 7 days of clicks with zero messages.
campaigns.compliance_note: Educational framing only. Not legal advice. Oraya never implies insurance licensure.

campaigns.objective: Lead gen forms to US insurance and dealership decision-makers from Frankie's profile, with his face and his licensed-producer credential, offering the Compliance-Safe AI Audit.
campaigns.hypothesis: LinkedIn's higher CPC is offset by its reported 6.1% average conversion rate against 3.75% for Google Search, producing a cost per qualified lead at or below Google Business Services CPL of $93.69.
campaigns.bid_model: CPC auction, Sponsored Content with Lead Gen Forms
campaigns.budget_note: Tier C: $400. Benchmarks: CPC $5 to $8, median CPM $31, CTR 0.44% to 0.65%, Lead Gen Form CPL $75 to $150 at 6% to 10% form conversion. At $400 expect 3 to 5 leads.
campaigns.audience: US insurance agency principals and owners, dealership general managers and BDC directors. Job title and seniority targeting, US only.
campaigns.creative: See ads/creative-briefs.md, brief 4. Frankie's face, his credential stated as his own.
campaigns.landing: LinkedIn Lead Gen Form, routed to the Compliance-Safe AI Audit. Fulfilment happens on the platform the conversation started on.
campaigns.kill_rule: Kill if CPL exceeds $150 over 2 weeks, or if leads arrive but none book the audit call. At 0.44% to 0.65% CTR a single week produces too little signal to judge, so the review window is 2 weeks, not 1.
campaigns.compliance_note: Frankie's producer licence is stated as his own credential, with the boundary explicit. Oraya is not a licensed entity and never implies otherwise.

campaigns.objective: Buy impressions on the vertical keywords once ranking is forming, and read which search terms actually convert.
campaigns.hypothesis: At a $450 package netting $360, the ROI ceiling is $72 per order. At a $0.50 CPC and 5% conversion the real cost is about $10 per order, so the campaign should be strongly profitable. One week of spend proves or disproves the conversion half.
campaigns.eligibility: NOT ELIGIBLE in the first 30 days. Fiverr does not publish the gate. Third-party sources put it at Level 1 plus about 20 completed orders in some categories, or Level 2 for full access, and they disagree. New gigs are ineligible until they have conversion data. Verify inside the seller dashboard and log the answer before planning spend.
campaigns.bid_model: Cost-per-click auction. Fiverr calculates the minimum per-click amount needed to win over other ads. Daily budget controlled by the seller. Payment is retrospective, withdrawn monthly from Fiverr earnings.
campaigns.budget_note: $3 to $5 a day for two to three weeks when it opens. Typical CPCs $0.10 to $2.00. ROI rule: cost per order below 20% of net earnings per order.
campaigns.audience: Fiverr search traffic on the gig's own keyword set
campaigns.creative: The gig's own images and video. Promoted Gigs reuses the listing, so improving the ad means improving the listing.
campaigns.kill_rule: Pause if 7 days of spend produce clicks and zero messages, or if cost per message exceeds 10% of the $450 Basic price, meaning $45.

campaigns.objective: Test whether compliance-framed cold calling converts paid traffic at all, on a keyword surface where no competitor mentions consent, DNC, quiet hours or disclosure.
campaigns.hypothesis: The compliance framing converts paid Fiverr traffic at a higher rate than the generic tool framing, because 2,232 competing services on ai-cold-calling say nothing about any of it.
campaigns.eligibility: Same unverified gate as fvr-promoted-gig1, and the same answer: not in month 1.
campaigns.budget_note: $3 to $5 a day, and not in the same week as fvr-promoted-gig1.
campaigns.audience: Fiverr search traffic on ai-cold-calling and ai-sdr-agent keywords
campaigns.kill_rule: Same as gig1, at the $350 Audit price, meaning a $35 cost-per-message ceiling. Never run gig1 and gig2 promotion in the same week at launch: two variables moving at once means neither result is attributable.

campaigns.objective: Retarget gig visitors and dashboard-demo viewers, and build a lookalike from audit leads.
campaigns.hypothesis: Retargeting converts at a materially lower cost per message than prospecting, which is the normal shape, but it is worth nothing until there is an audience to retarget.
campaigns.eligibility: n/a. Requires a pixel and a lead volume that does not exist yet.
campaigns.budget_note: Part of the Tier D $2,000 Meta line. Worth nothing in month 1 and a lot in month 3. Do not fund it early.
campaigns.audience: Gig visitors, dashboard-demo viewers, and a lookalike built from Compliance-Safe AI Audit leads.
campaigns.kill_rule: Do not start until the source audience exceeds 300 people. Below that the audience is too small to serve and the spend buys frequency against a handful of people.
